headline: Majors hold above 200-day lines but lack conviction; funding crowded and expensive on the long side while whales rotate into cold storage.
paragraphs: The regime is mixed but leaning constructive on structure alone. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all trade above their 200-day moving averages; only Dogecoin and Cardano have fallen below. The golden cross, a 50-day line crossing above the 200-day line, is present in Ethereum and Solana, a mild structural bullish signal. Bitcoin lacks the cross; its MACD has already rolled below its signal line, a sign momentum is cooling even as price holds the long-term trend. Ethereum and XRP also show MACD below signal. Only Solana prints MACD above signal, the sole major holding momentum acceleration into trend. The picture is therefore a market that has climbed back above its long-term support but is not showing widespread conviction to push higher.

The monthly window reveals the real tension. Over the last 30 days, Bitcoin up 15.3 percent, Ethereum up 23.3 percent, Solana up 25.4 percent, XRP up 15.8 percent, Dogecoin up 10.7 percent, and Cardano up 12.2 percent. But over the week, Bitcoin down 1.3 percent, Ethereum down 3.4 percent, XRP down 13.0 percent, Dogecoin down 13.1 percent, and Cardano down 14.1 percent. Only Solana up 2.7 percent on the week. The monthly rally is being tested and partly reversed in real time. RSI values across the board sit between 48 and 63: Bitcoin 62.7, Ethereum 60.1, Solana 59.6, BNB 61.8. These are elevated but not extreme; they flag momentum is present without screaming overbought. Cardano and Dogecoin lag at 48.4 and 51.5, signals of fatigue in the weakest assets.

Positioning on leverage exchanges reveals an asymmetric crowd. Bitcoin long-short ratio sits at 1.29, meaning longs outnumber shorts by a 29 percent margin, and funding is positive (0.49 percent annualized at 5.3 percent). Ethereum is far more crowded: 1.63 long-short ratio with 5.6 basis points of 8-hour funding, implying 6.2 percent annualized carry for holding the long. Over the last 3 to 4 hours, $1.3 million in long liquidations hit Ethereum against only $195,000 in shorts: a signal longs are being squeezed. Solana is an outlier, funding negative at minus 6.0 percent annualized (shorts are paying), yet the long-short ratio is 1.95, the second most skewed long position in the set. The deepest skew belongs to Dogecoin: 4.17 ratio with 9.8 percent annualized funding and a cascade of $208,000 longs liquidated in 11 hours versus $48,000 shorts. This is a fragile structure: the crowd has paid a lot to hold long positions, especially in altcoins, and any reversal will draw liquidity orders from forced selling. Bitcoin and Ethereum carry expensive, crowded longs; Solana and Dogecoin are even more exposed.

Flows paint a picture of rotation and caution. Over the week ending September 2, $344 million moved off exchanges (into custody or cold wallets), a positive marker that holders are taking coins to safety. But this reverses three prior weeks: week ending August 26 saw $1,511 million move onto exchanges, and the week before, $1,000 million. The most recent print is a break in that trend but is too fresh to call a regime shift. On US spot ETF flows, Bitcoin saw a $236.5 million outflow on September 1 alone, but the five-session net is still positive at $252.8 million, meaning one heavy redemption is not yet a break. Ethereum, by contrast, shows no conflict: $8.6 million in on September 1 with 10 consecutive days of same-direction inflows (net $616.5 million over five sessions). The stablecoin float remains broad at $309 billion, up 1.16 percent over 30 days, supplying ample dry powder for demand when it arrives. Stablecoins onto Coinbase total $100 million in the 24-hour window, modest volume suggesting no panic or euphoric rush at this moment.

Sentiment reads at 63, labeled Greed, with a 30-day range from 25 to 74. This is the high end of a wide swung range, placing the crowd in the upper half of confidence while leaving room for it to climb further. Yet the tape shows precision where emotion would suggest recklessness: the tape shows a crowd that paid for long levered positions but is now seeing the monthly rally tested on a weekly horizon, with some rotation into custody and some lightening via ETF redemption. The disagreement between the monthly climb and the weekly slide, and between elevated RSI values and cooling MACD signals, is the read: the move has been strong enough to draw leverage and set a cautious mood, but not strong enough to hold every position when tested. The broad support of the 200-day averages has not been reclaimed as a launchpad; it is being defended.

Watch for three signals of regime change. First, a sustained break of the 200-day lines in BTC, ETH, or SOL would indicate the long-term support has failed. Second, a flip in weekly net whale flows back onto exchanges (reversing the latest week's $344 million off-move) would signal profit-taking or fear at the margin. Third, a collapse of the long-short ratios in Bitcoin or Ethereum paired with a spike in liquidations would confirm the crowded longs are cracking. For now, the structure holds, but it is being tested at both the week and the funding layer.
